arguments.text: Fixed. `dayjs.tz(input, tz)` was always treating its input as a wall-clock time in the target zone (`d.utc(input).valueOf()`), so an instant (Date/timestamp/Day.js object) got re-interpreted as wall time and shifted by the zone offset. Non-string inputs are now converted instead of re-parsed: `dayjs.tz(d, 'America/Vancouver').format()` → `2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00`, same for a timestamp and for a Day.js object, matching moment-timezone. String inputs are untouched. Full suite still green (524/524).

Fixed. In `proto.tz` the offset was derived from an unrounded minute diff, so a fractional second leaked into the offset (`+08:59.9956…`). The diff is now rounded to whole minutes, and the milliseconds of the instant are carried over so the conversion still preserves the exact instant. `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')` → `+09:00` (valueOf/`SSS` still `…690258`/`258`, like moment). Full suite green (524/524).

Fixed. The `nl` locale's ordinal was a hard-coded `n => `${n}.``. It now picks the Dutch suffix by number (`1`/`8`/`>=20` → `ste`, otherwise `de`) and bracket-escapes it so the letters aren't re-parsed as format tokens (same technique as `en-gb`/`sv`). `format('Do')` now gives `1ste`, `8ste`, `19de`, `20ste`, `31ste` — identical to moment for every day 1–31. Full suite green (524/524).

Fixed. `weekYear()` only handled the December→next-year case; it never handled early January dates that belong to the last week of the previous week-year. It now returns `year - 1` when the month is January and the week number is 52 or 53, so `dayjs('2021-01-01').locale('en-gb').weekYear()` → `2020` (also 01-02, 01-03) while `2021-01-04` → `2021`. Verified against moment for every day of 2015–2026 in both `en` and `en-gb`. Full suite green (524/524).

Non-string inputs are now converted instead of re-parsed: `dayjs.tz(new Date('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00'), 'America/Vancouver').format()` → `2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00`, and the same for a timestamp and for a Day.js object, matching moment-timezone. arguments.text: Confirmed: the customParseFormat plugin's `A`/`a` tokens only accept literal `AM`/`PM`, so a locale meridiem like zh-cn's `凌晨`/`下午` fails to match and the parse throws internally → Invalid Date. I'm making the meridiem token locale-aware (using the locale's `meridiem` function, like moment does) and will verify the round trip. ETA ~6 min.

  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').subtract(1, 'ms').toISOString()).toBe('P0D')
  expect(dayjs.duration({ milliseconds: 5 }).toISOString()).toBe('PT0.005S')
  expect(dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').humanize()).toBe(dayjs.duration(1).humanize())
})

arguments.text: Fixed. The `A`/`a` tokens were hard-wired to the literal `AM`/`PM`, so a locale meridiem (`凌晨`, `下午`, …) never matched and the internal match threw → Invalid Date. The tokens now match a word and resolve it through the locale's `meridiem` function (like moment), so the round trip works: `dayjs('2018年5月2日凌晨1点02分03秒', 'YYYY年M月D日Ah点mm分ss秒', 'zh-cn').format('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss')` → `2018-05-02 01:02:03`, and the afternoon case (`下午1点`) → `13:02:03`. Verified against moment for AM/PM/midnight/noon/23:59 and for `en`/`ja`. Full suite green (524/524).

Fixed. The duration plugin's `unitToMS` table had no `milliseconds` entry, so `1 * undefined` produced NaN and the duration came out empty. Added `milliseconds: 1`, so `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms').toISOString()` → `PT0.001S` (same as `dayjs.duration(1)` and as moment), and `asMilliseconds()`/`milliseconds()`/`add(1, 'ms')`/`subtract(1, 'ms')` all work. Full suite green (524/524).
